records.title: Observations on Simulated 12-Second Decompressions to 32,000 Feet
records.citation: Barron CI, Collier DR Jr, Cook TJ. Observations on Simulated 12-Second Decompressions to 32,000 Feet. J Aviat Med. 1958;29(8):563–574.
records.period: Study initiated August 1956. End date unreported.
records.locator: Introduction p. 563, Results pp. 566 and 568–570, Tables II–V (PDF pp. 7–8), Summary p. 574
records.note: Twenty-nine flights and 154 exposure records in Table II. Distinct headcount and whether a repeat instructor is included in the table are unresolved. Hypoxia reactions appear as 88 in the text and sum to 89 in Table V. The paper gives no clinical DCS tally or systematic DCS follow-up.

records.title: Acute Hypoxia During Rapid Decompression and Emergency Descent in a Commercial Jet Aircraft
records.study_label: Ohio State simulated cabin decompression and descent
records.citation: Donaldson RT, Carter ET, Billings CE Jr, Hitchcock FA. Acute hypoxia during rapid decompression and emergency descent in a commercial jet aircraft. Aerosp Med. 1960;31(10):842–851.
records.locator: Results pp. 844–848 and Summary p. 850 (PDF pp. 3–7 and 9)
records.note: The four oxygen conditions gave 35 chamber exposures in ten people. Two of seven no-oxygen tests did not complete the planned profile, one following severe hypoxia and the other following severe ear pain. The report separately describes repeat tests in three of the same people after alcohol. No clinical DCS tally is given.

trial_scopes.note: Four oxygen conditions. Participants repeated exposures. The summary count matches the two figure series.

trial_scopes.locator: Results and Figures 1–2, printed pp. 844–847 (PDF pp. 3–6)
trial_scopes.note: Gas schedule as reported. Delays are measured from ascending through the source trigger altitude. Participants can occur in more than one arm.
